steps.title: Rows and columns
steps.content: Most star and number patterns use an outer loop for rows and an inner loop for columns. The outer loop controls how many lines are printed; the inner loop controls what appears on one line.
steps.example: For 3 rows, the outer loop runs 3 times.

steps.title: Trace a rectangle
steps.prompt: An outer loop runs 3 times and an inner loop prints 4 stars each time. How many stars are printed?

steps.title: Build a right triangle
steps.content: A right triangle of height n prints row i with i stars. The inner loop's upper bound depends on the current row number.
steps.tip: Trace each row separately before generalizing the loop condition.

steps.title: Count the pattern
steps.prompt: A triangle has 5 rows and row i prints i stars. How many stars are printed in total?

steps.title: Use spaces for alignment
steps.content: Pyramids and centered patterns print spaces before stars. A common row i uses n−i leading spaces and 2i−1 stars. Keep spacing logic separate from star logic.
steps.example: For n=3, rows use (2 spaces,1 star), (1 space,3 stars), (0 spaces,5 stars).

questions.prompt: Which loop usually controls the number of rows?
questions.explanation: The outer loop typically advances from one row to the next.

questions.prompt: A 4×5 rectangle prints how many symbols?
questions.explanation: Four rows with five symbols each gives 4×5 = 20.

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, row i prints i stars. How many stars are in row 4?
questions.explanation: The row number equals the star count, so row 4 prints four stars.

questions.prompt: How many stars are printed by rows 1 through 4 of a triangle?
What controls the number of leading spaces in a centered pyramid?
options: The row's position relative to total height
questions.explanation: Earlier rows need more leading spaces to center the pattern.
